problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & -4 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 25 & 0 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?

examples.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
examples.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- $R_1 := \ldots$

- $R_3:=R_3-3R_2$

- $R_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
examples.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below $a_{22}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_1 := R_1 - 2R_2\quad$ and $\quad R_4:=R_4+2R_2.$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}.$
